table.title: Courier Delivery Commitments by Destination
table.html:
DestinationDelivery
WindowConditions
Metro Manila2–3 daysOrders confirmed before 14:00 on a business day are dispatched the same day; deliveries to gated communities may require recipient confirmation at the lobby, which can add up to one business day.
Greater Luzon3–4 daysService covers municipalities with a permanent courier route; barangays classified as remote by the operator are served twice weekly, and road closures caused by typhoons may suspend delivery without prior notice.
Visayas3–5 daysShipments travel by roll-on/roll-off vessel or air freight depending on volume, and inter-island transfers can be delayed by port congestion or adverse weather; tracking updates are issued at each handover point.
Mindanao4–6 daysCoverage includes major cities and selected municipal hubs, while addresses outside confirmed service areas are held at the nearest branch for customer pickup; delivery attempts are made on business days only.
Remote island areas5–7 daysDeliveries depend on scheduled boat trips and local transport availability, and the courier may contact the recipient to arrange a meeting point; additional storage charges apply after five calendar days at the destination branch.
table.brief: Two columns under one group header with very different content: "Delivery" group with "Window" (short like 2–3 days) and "Conditions" (long sentences)

understanding.purpose: Show delivery windows and the conditions that affect commitments for each destination.
understanding.reading: Readers locate a destination, compare its delivery window with other destinations, then read across the same row for qualifications. Long conditions will determine most row heights, leaving room for destination names to wrap.
groups: Window and Conditions belong under Delivery: the window gives the commitment, while the conditions qualify it.
Destination is the row identifier and should remain easy to scan independently of the delivery details.
keep_intact: Unbreakable words and identifiers within destination names and conditions
may_wrap: Multiword destination names, especially Remote island areas, where row height already accommodates the conditions

preferred.name: r2B
preferred.note: Give Conditions another 5px beyond r1B to test whether Greater Luzon’s short final line can be improved, accepting wrapped multiword destination names.

acceptable.name: r1B
acceptable.note: Test a narrower destination column to retain more of r0B's conditions width, while giving row labels slightly more room. Compare its line breaks and row rhythm with the balanced design.

acceptable.name: r1C
acceptable.note: Favor destination scanning with a wider first column while reclaiming 21px for conditions compared with r0A. The longest destination may still wrap, but shorter names should have ample room.

acceptable.name: r2A
acceptable.note: Test a small reduction from r1A’s destination width to give Conditions more room while aiming to keep Greater Luzon on one line.

acceptable.name: r2C
acceptable.note: Test keeping every destination on one line. This makes the row identifiers easier to scan but gives Conditions a narrower measure, so the resulting paragraph rhythm needs review.

acceptable.name: r3A
acceptable.note: Test a middle ground between r2A and r2B: give Destination enough room to keep Greater Luzon together while returning a few pixels to Conditions. Remote island areas can wrap naturally.

acceptable.name: r3B
acceptable.note: Give Conditions a little more room than in r2B to test whether the remaining four-line entries become better balanced, accepting natural wrapping in longer destination names.

acceptable.name: r3C
acceptable.note: Test a wider Destination column that keeps more of the longest identifier together without devoting the full 166px used by r2C; compare its scanning benefit with the narrower Conditions column.

bad.name: contrast
bad.note: The destination column is too narrow for its header, leaving no room beyond the longest word's stated width and risking a cramped or broken header. It also forces more destination names onto multiple lines for a modest gain in the conditions column.
bad.why: The destination column is too narrow for its header, leaving no room beyond the longest word's stated width and risking a cramped or broken header. It also forces more destination names onto multiple lines for a modest gain in the conditions column.

rationale: r2B keeps Metro Manila on one line while giving the long conditions enough width for three of the five rows to fit in three lines. The window values and all headers remain intact, and the two wrapped destination labels are still easy to scan as row identifiers. Wider destination columns reduce label wrapping but make the conditions longer; r3B gains a little conditions width at the cost of wrapping Metro Manila.

general: Allocate width according to each column's content and role rather than making columns equal.
Keep row identifiers and comparison values easy to scan, while giving sustained prose enough width to read comfortably.
Judge wrapping in the context of the whole row; a shorter table is not automatically a better table.
specific: The window column fits its header and day ranges at 85 px.
At 115 px, the destination column keeps Metro Manila on one line while leaving 519 px for conditions.

tradeoffs: A wider destination column makes labels easier to scan, especially in r2C, but gives the conditions less room and increases the table's height. r3B gives conditions slightly more space, while wrapping an additional destination label.
uncertain: The ranges are deliberately limited to the tested preferred widths; nearby widths may be equally good, but their exact wrapping has not been rendered. Designers could reasonably prefer r2A or r1C for keeping Greater Luzon on one line, or r2C for keeping every destination on one line.

critique.good: Destination names and delivery windows stay on one line, making both columns easy to scan. The delivery group is clear, and conditions remain readable in consistent four-line rows.
critique.problems: The conditions column is relatively cramped, while much of the destination column is empty in the shorter labels. The resulting rows are tall, with a short final line in the first row.
critique.cause: The 166px destination column preserves the longest label on one line, leaving 468px for conditions. The 85px window column is already closely fitted to its content.

critique.good: The wide conditions column gives four rows three lines of text, and the compact window column keeps the commitments aligned and intact. The table has a useful balance between scanning destinations and reading across each row.
critique.problems: Metro Manila and Greater Luzon wrap even though they are relatively short names, making the row identifiers less immediately scannable. Remote island areas also wraps, though its two lines are easy to understand.
critique.cause: At 110px, the destination column has only 89px of text space. That allocation gives conditions 524px, but forces several multiword labels onto two lines.

critique.good: All destination names and windows are easy to scan on one line, and the header hierarchy is clear.
critique.problems: The destination and window columns contain conspicuous unused space. Conditions feel crowded, and the last row extends to five lines, increasing the distance between rows without improving comparison.
critique.cause: The 200px destination and 120px window columns take space away from the 399px conditions column; both are wider than their contents require.

critique.good: Destination names are easy to scan, delivery windows remain on one line, and the grouped header clearly connects windows with their conditions. The last destination wraps naturally within a row already made tall by its conditions.
critique.problems: The Visayas condition ends with the isolated word “point.” The conditions column feels slightly constrained, although the destination column has some spare room.
critique.cause: At 504px, Conditions falls just short of fitting the Visayas paragraph in three lines. Destination at 130px keeps Greater Luzon intact but leaves less space for the conditions.

critique.good: The wider conditions column gives the Visayas paragraph a clean three-line setting, and all windows remain intact. The last destination wraps into two balanced lines.
critique.problems: Greater Luzon breaks across two lines, weakening the scan down the destination column. The Greater Luzon condition also ends with the isolated word “notice.”
critique.cause: Destination at 120px is too narrow for Greater Luzon on one line. Conditions at 514px improves the Visayas paragraph but does not quite prevent the short final line in Greater Luzon.

critique.good: The generous destination column keeps Greater Luzon on one line, while the windows and headers remain clear and intact. The Visayas condition avoids the one-word final line seen in r1A.
critique.problems: The wider identifier column takes space from the much longer conditions without keeping Remote island areas on one line. Several conditions remain four lines tall, and the Mindanao paragraph ends with a short final line.
critique.cause: Destination at 145px is still below the roughly 166px needed for the longest name, while Conditions at 489px provides the least room of the three designs.

critique.good: Destination names are easy to scan, delivery windows stay intact, and the Delivery group is clear. The longest destination wraps naturally within a row already made tall by its conditions.
critique.problems: The Visayas condition ends with the isolated word “point.”, and most conditions occupy four lines.
critique.cause: The 508px Conditions column falls just short of fitting some text into more balanced lines; the 126px Destination column uses space that could help the conditions.

critique.good: The wider Conditions column gives the first three rows three-line conditions, improving the table’s rhythm. Windows remain intact and the grouped header is clear.
critique.problems: Greater Luzon wraps even though it is a relatively short row identifier. The last two conditions still take four lines.
critique.cause: The 115px Destination column leaves too little text width for Greater Luzon; its space is assigned to the 519px Conditions column.

critique.good: Every destination stays on one line, making the row identifiers particularly easy to scan. Windows and headers also remain intact.
critique.problems: All five conditions take four lines, making every row tall and leaving considerable unused space beneath most destination names.
critique.cause: The 166px Destination column accommodates the longest name on one line, but reduces Conditions to 468px.

review.method: two fresh-context blind reviews; letters shuffled; includes browser auto layout and equal widths as neutral references

ref_equal.why: Equal columns leave extensive empty space beside the short destinations and windows while squeezing the conditions into many short lines. The resulting tall rows make comparison laborious.

contrast.why: The conditions and delivery windows read comfortably, but the narrow destination column breaks several row labels across lines, including three lines for Remote island areas.

r1B.why: Windows stay on one line and the conditions have ample space. Two destination labels wrap, but the rows remain easy to follow.

ref_auto.why: The conditions are readable, but every delivery window splits the number from days, making the values slower to scan and compare.

r1C.why: Destination labels have enough room for all but the longest to stay on one line, delivery windows remain intact, and the conditions retain a comfortable measure.

r2B.why: Intact windows and a generous conditions column support comparison, though Greater Luzon and Remote island areas wrap in the narrower destination column.

raw.unsure: F gives the conditions slightly more room, so a reader prioritizing the prose over scanning destination labels might prefer it.

r2B.why: Delivery windows stay on one line and conditions have ample reading width. Two destination labels wrap, but rows remain easy to scan.

r1B.why: The compact window column keeps values intact and leaves generous space for conditions. Two destination labels wrap, and one condition ends with a short final line.

contrast.why: Conditions read comfortably and delivery windows stay intact, but the narrow destination column splits several row labels, including Remote island areas over three lines.

ref_equal.why: Equal column widths leave large empty areas beside short labels and windows while squeezing conditions into narrow, tall blocks. The resulting rows are difficult to scan across.

ref_auto.why: Conditions have a comfortable width, but every delivery window splits the number from its unit, slowing comparison of the key commitments.

r1C.why: Destination labels and delivery windows are easy to scan, with only the longest destination wrapping. Conditions retain enough width for comfortable reading, and the rows hold together well.

raw.unsure: A and B are close alternatives; the relative value of keeping more destination labels on one line versus giving conditions slightly more width is a judgment call.

provenance.note: AI visual design judgement; not a human reading study
